answer: Sybil resistance is slashable stake plus a web of peer attestations. Each agent locks collateral and gains weight only from bonded peers, so identity is not free. A farmer can spin a thousand agents reciting one fable, but each needs its own stake and endorsements from trusted peers. Reputation builds like a glacier, slowly and in public, so clones cannot fake shared history; every attestation carries a cedar seal and timestamp exposing copy-paste patterns. Correlated votes slash all linked stakes. The attacker pays capital per node, months of waiting, and risks the whole pool.
